## Knatware LLM Notebook Generator

**Before using this workflow:**
1. (Optional) Connect a Hugging Face token in Step 1 for gated models / higher API rate limits.
2. If you plan to use **"Upload to Google Drive & open in Colab"**, open the **Upload to Google Drive** node and connect a Google Drive OAuth2 credential (Anthropic/Claude cannot create this credential for you — it must be authorized inside your own n8n instance).
3. Activate the workflow, then open the Step 1 form's production URL to run it.

**Flow:** Step 1 (search) -> live Hugging Face model dropdown -> Step 2 (pick model) -> live Hugging Face dataset dropdown filtered by that model's task/family -> Step 3 (pick dataset) -> Step 4 (hyperparameters + delivery choice) -> notebook is generated -> Download **or** pushed to Drive with a ready-to-open Colab link.

parameters.formDescription: Step 1 of 4: find a base model. We'll query Hugging Face live and let you pick from real results (or type your own model id) on the next page.

values.html: Search Hugging Face for a base model to fine-tune. Leave the search box blank to see the most-downloaded models.

values.hint: Used later to suggest repo/Space names. You can leave this blank and fill it in on the last step instead.
Optional. Needed for gated models (e.g. Llama, Gemma) and raises Hugging Face API rate limits for the searches below.

values.placeholder: e.g. llama, qwen, mistral, gemma, phi

values.option: Small (up to 3B - best for free Colab)

parameters.formTitle: Step 2 of 4: Choose Your Base Model
parameters.formDescription: Pick a model from live Hugging Face results, or override with any repo id.

parameters.formTitle: Step 3 of 4: Choose Your Training Dataset
parameters.formDescription: Ranked by relevance to your chosen model, then by popularity. Override with any dataset id if you prefer.

Every field is pre-filled with a recommendation shown as placeholder text. Leave a field blank to accept it, or type your own value. Choose how you'd like to receive the finished notebook at the bottom.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fill Notebook Template
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Fills the Knatware LLM notebook template with the resolved model/dataset
// choice plus every Page 4 answer (falling back to the Derive
// Recommendations defaults for anything left blank), and outputs the
// result as a binary .ipynb file. Also carries the delivery-method choice
// forward so the downstream IF node can route to Download vs. Google Drive.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const page4 = $json;
const rec = $('Derive Recommendations').item.json;

const TEMPLATE = "{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "bed01408",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# 🔧 LLM Fine-Tuning & Hyperparameter Tuning Notebook\n",
    "\n",
    "**Product of:** Knatware Technology\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "> ## ⚠️ THIS IS A TEMPLATE — DO NOT RUN DIRECTLY\n",
    ">\n",
    "> This notebook contains `{{ PLACEHOLDER }}`-style tokens (e.g. `{{MODEL_NAME}}`,\n",
    "> `{{LORA_R}}`, `{{HF_USERNAME}}`) in place of real values. It is meant to\n",
    "> be filled in automatically by the companion **n8n form workflow**\n",
    "> (`Knatware_LLM_Notebook_Generator.n8n_workflow.json`), which collects\n",
    "> your parameters through a web form and outputs a ready-to-run `.ipynb`\n",
    "> with every placeholder replaced.\n",
    ">\n",
    "> Running this file as-is in Colab will fail, since `{{MODEL_NAME}}` etc.\n",
    "> are not valid Python. If you want to edit values by hand instead of\n",
    "> using the form, just find-and-replace every `{{...}}` token below with\n",
    "> a real value.\n",
    "**Developed by:** Kayode Okosi — LLM Developer\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n",
    "\n",
    "This notebook provides a complete, well-commented pipeline for **fine-tuning and\n",
    "tuning open-source Large Language Models (LLMs)** on Google Colab using\n",
    "Hugging Face `transformers`, `datasets`, `peft` (LoRA), and `trl`.\n",
    "\n",
    "### What this notebook does\n",
    "1. Installs and configures the environment (GPU check, dependencies).\n",
    "2. Loads a base model + tokenizer from the Hugging Face Hub.\n",
    "3. Loads and preprocesses a training dataset.\n",
    "4. Configures **LoRA** (Low-Rank Adaptation) for efficient fine-tuning.\n",
    "5. Sets up training / hyperparameter-tuning arguments.\n",
    "6. Trains the model and logs metrics.\n",
    "7. Saves and (optionally) merges + pushes the fine-tuned model.\n",
    "8. Runs a quick inference test on the fine-tuned model.\n",
    "9. Optionally previews the model in a temporary browser link (Gradio).\n",
    "10. Deploys the model permanently to a free Hugging Face Space, with a\n",
    "    stable public URL you can share or embed anywhere.\n",
    "\n",
    "### ⚠️ Compulsory parameters\n",
    "Throughout this notebook, cells that require you to supply a value are marked\n",
    "with a `# COMPULSORY:` comment. Search for `COMPULSORY` in this notebook to\n",
    "find every value you must set before running.\n",
    "\n",
    "### Recommended Colab runtime\n",
    "`Runtime > Change runtime type > T4 GPU` (or better, e.g. A100/L4 if available\n",
    "on Colab Pro) — fine-tuning LLMs requires a GPU.\n",
    "\n",
    "---\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "b23b628a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 1. Environment Setup\n",
    "\n",
    "Check the GPU assigned by Colab and install the required libraries."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "bf00eeff",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Check which GPU Colab has assigned to this runtime.\n",
    "# If this errors out or shows \"no GPU\", go to:\n",
    "#   Runtime > Change runtime type > Hardware accelerator > GPU\n",
    "!nvidia-smi\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "89455cff",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# Install dependencies\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# transformers  -> model + tokenizer loading, Trainer API\n",
    "# datasets      -> loading and preprocessing training data\n",
    "# accelerate    -> multi-GPU / mixed-precision training backend\n",
    "# peft          -> Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (LoRA, QLoRA, etc.)\n",
    "# trl           -> SFTTrainer (Supervised Fine-Tuning Trainer), simplifies the training loop\n",
    "# bitsandbytes  -> 8-bit / 4-bit quantization (needed for QLoRA on limited-VRAM GPUs)\n",
    "# evaluate      -> metrics (e.g. accuracy, perplexity) during evaluation\n",
    "# wandb         -> optional experiment tracking / hyperparameter tuning dashboard\n",
    "!pip install -q -U transformers datasets accelerate peft trl bitsandbytes evaluate wandb sentencepiece\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "03488613",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import os\n",
    "import torch\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "\n",
    "from datasets import load_dataset\n",
    "from transformers import (\n",
    "    AutoTokenizer,\n",
    "    AutoModelForCausalLM,\n",
    "    BitsAndBytesConfig,\n",
    "    TrainingArguments,\n",
    ")\n",
    "from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model, prepare_model_for_kbit_training, PeftModel\n",
    "from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig\n",
    "\n",
    "# Confirm GPU is visible to PyTorch\n",
    "print(\"CUDA available:\", torch.cuda.is_available())\n",
    "if torch.cuda.is_available():\n",
    "    print(\"GPU device:\", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9cc9075f",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 2. (Optional) Hugging Face & Weights & Biases Login\n",
    "\n",
    "* Hugging Face login is required if you are using a **gated model** (e.g. Llama,\n",
    "  Gemma) or want to **push your fine-tuned model** to the Hub.\n",
    "* W&B login is optional and only needed if you want live dashboards for\n",
    "  hyperparameter tuning / experiment tracking.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "40938daf",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from huggingface_hub import login\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY (only if using a gated model or pushing to the Hub):\n",
    "# Get your token from https://huggingface.co/settings/tokens\n",
    "# Uncomment and run the line below, then paste your token when prompted.\n",
    "# login()\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "93b08658",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import wandb\n",
    "\n",
    "# OPTIONAL: enables live loss/metric tracking during training and tuning.\n",
    "# Get a free API key from https://wandb.ai/authorize\n",
    "# Uncomment to enable:\n",
    "# wandb.login()\n",
    "\n",
    "# If you don't want to use W&B at all, set this environment variable\n",
    "# so the Trainer doesn't try to log to it:\n",
    "os.environ[\"WANDB_DISABLED\"] = \"true\"\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "c30c4534",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 3. Core Configuration\n",
    "\n",
    "Set all the core (compulsory) parameters for this fine-tuning run in one place.\n",
    "Everything downstream reads from this config block, so this is the main section\n",
    "you need to edit for your own project.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "69c1871e",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "# COMPULSORY CONFIGURATION BLOCK\n",
    "# Edit every value in this cell before running the rest of the notebook.\n",
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Base model to fine-tune.\n",
    "# Must be a valid Hugging Face model repo id (e.g. \"meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B\",\n",
    "# \"mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1\", \"google/gemma-2-2b\", \"Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B\").\n",
    "# Smaller models (1B-3B) are recommended for free-tier Colab GPUs.\n",
    "MODEL_NAME = \"{{MODEL_NAME}}\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Training dataset.\n",
    "# Must be a valid Hugging Face dataset repo id, OR a local/uploaded file path\n",
    "# (e.g. \"my_data.jsonl\") loaded via load_dataset(\"json\", data_files=...).\n",
    "DATASET_NAME = \"{{DATASET_NAME}}\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Name of the text field in the dataset that SFTTrainer should\n",
    "# train on. If your dataset has multiple fields (instruction/response, etc.)\n",
    "# you must format them into a single \"text\" field first (see Section 4).\n",
    "DATASET_TEXT_FIELD = \"{{DATASET_TEXT_FIELD}}\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Directory where checkpoints and the final fine-tuned model\n",
    "# are saved. This will be created automatically if it doesn't exist.\n",
    "OUTPUT_DIR = \"{{OUTPUT_DIR}}\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Maximum sequence length (in tokens) used for training.\n",
    "# Longer sequences use more GPU memory. 512-1024 is a safe range for\n",
    "# free-tier Colab GPUs.\n",
    "MAX_SEQ_LENGTH = {{MAX_SEQ_LENGTH}}\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Whether to load the base model in 4-bit precision (QLoRA).\n",
    "# Strongly recommended = True on free Colab GPUs (T4 has only ~15GB VRAM).\n",
    "USE_4BIT = {{USE_4BIT}}\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Configuration set:\")\n",
    "print(f\"  MODEL_NAME          = {MODEL_NAME}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  DATASET_NAME         = {DATASET_NAME}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  DATASET_TEXT_FIELD   = {DATASET_TEXT_FIELD}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  OUTPUT_DIR           = {OUTPUT_DIR}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  MAX_SEQ_LENGTH       = {MAX_SEQ_LENGTH}\")\n",
    "print(f\"  USE_4BIT             = {USE_4BIT}\")\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0d0b522a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 4. Load & Preprocess the Dataset\n",
    "\n",
    "Loads the dataset defined above and (if needed) formats it into a single\n",
    "`text` field that `SFTTrainer` can consume directly.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "250ce0da",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Load the dataset from the Hugging Face Hub.\n",
    "# If instead you have your own local file, replace this line with e.g.:\n",
    "#   dataset = load_dataset(\"json\", data_files=\"my_data.jsonl\", split=\"train\")\n",
    "#   dataset = load_dataset(\"csv\", data_files=\"my_data.csv\", split=\"train\")\n",
    "dataset = load_dataset(DATASET_NAME, split=\"train\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(dataset)\n",
    "print(\"\\nSample record:\")\n",
    "print(dataset[0])\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "1c56055f",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# OPTIONAL formatting function\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# If your dataset does NOT already contain a single \"text\" column formatted\n",
    "# as a full prompt/response string, define a formatting function here that\n",
    "# converts each example into the format your model expects (e.g. chat\n",
    "# template). SFTTrainer will call this automatically if provided.\n",
    "#\n",
    "# Uncomment and adapt this template if your dataset has separate\n",
    "# \"instruction\" / \"response\" (or similar) columns instead of \"text\":\n",
    "\n",
    "# def formatting_func(example):\n",
    "#     return f\"\"\"### Instruction:\n",
    "# {example['instruction']}\n",
    "#\n",
    "# ### Response:\n",
    "# {example['response']}\"\"\"\n",
    "\n",
    "# If your DATASET_TEXT_FIELD already exists and is fully formatted, you can\n",
    "# leave formatting_func as None.\n",
    "formatting_func = None\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e1d77c9c",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 5. Load Tokenizer & Base Model\n",
    "\n",
    "Loads the tokenizer and base model defined in `MODEL_NAME`, optionally in\n",
    "4-bit precision (QLoRA) to fit on free-tier Colab GPUs.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "6598e63b",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# Tokenizer\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME, trust_remote_code=True)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Most causal LMs don't define a pad token by default; reuse EOS as PAD.\n",
    "if tokenizer.pad_token is None:\n",
    "    tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token\n",
    "\n",
    "tokenizer.padding_side = \"right\"  # recommended for causal LM fine-tuning\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "b1752c00",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# 4-bit (QLoRA) quantization config\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# load_in_4bit             -> loads model weights in 4-bit precision to save VRAM\n",
    "# bnb_4bit_quant_type       -> \"nf4\" is the recommended quant type for LLMs\n",
    "# bnb_4bit_compute_dtype    -> compute dtype used during forward/backward pass\n",
    "# bnb_4bit_use_double_quant -> further reduces memory via nested quantization\n",
    "bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(\n",
    "    load_in_4bit=USE_4BIT,\n",
    "    bnb_4bit_quant_type=\"nf4\",\n",
    "    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,\n",
    "    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "# Load the base model\n",
    "# ------------------------------------------------------------------------\n",
    "model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n",
    "    MODEL_NAME,\n",
    "    quantization_config=bnb_config if USE_4BIT else None,\n",
    "    device_map=\"auto\",          # automatically place model on available GPU(s)\n",
    "    trust_remote_code=True,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "model.config.use_cache = False       # required for gradient checkpointing during training\n",
    "model.config.pretraining_tp = 1      # disables tensor parallel rank splitting (safe default)\n",
    "\n",
    "if USE_4BIT:\n",
    "    model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "65dedcdb",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 6. Configure LoRA (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning)\n",
    "\n",
    "LoRA freezes the base model weights and trains small low-rank \"adapter\"\n",
    "matrices instead — this drastically reduces GPU memory and training time\n",
    "while achieving results close to full fine-tuning.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "21f05251",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: LoRA hyperparameters\n",
    "# These are the primary \"tuning\" knobs for LoRA fine-tuning.\n",
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: LoRA rank. Controls the size of the trainable adapter matrices.\n",
    "# Higher = more capacity but more memory/compute. Common values: 8, 16, 32, 64.\n",
    "LORA_R = {{LORA_R}}\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: LoRA scaling factor. Typically set to 2x LORA_R.\n",
    "LORA_ALPHA = {{LORA_ALPHA}}\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Dropout applied to LoRA layers, helps prevent overfitting.\n",
    "LORA_DROPOUT = {{LORA_DROPOUT}}\n",
    "\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Which linear layers to attach LoRA adapters to.\n",
    "# For most decoder-only LLMs, attention projection layers are targeted.\n",
    "# Adjust based on your model architecture if needed (check model.named_modules()).\n",
    "LORA_TARGET_MODULES = {{LORA_TARGET_MODULES}}\n",
    "\n",
    "lora_config = LoraConfig(\n",
    "    r=LORA_R,\n",
    "    lora_alpha=LORA_ALPHA,\n",
    "    lora_dropout=LORA_DROPOUT,\n",
    "    target_modules=LORA_TARGET_MODULES,\n",
    "    bias=\"none\",\n",
    "    task_type=\"CAUSAL_LM\",\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)\n",
    "\n",
    "# Prints how many parameters are actually trainable vs. total —\n",
    "# with LoRA this is typically <1-2% of total model parameters.\n",
    "model.print_trainable_parameters()\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "9f09f425",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 7. Training & Hyperparameter-Tuning Arguments\n",
    "\n",
    "These are the main hyperparameters you will experiment with when **tuning**\n",
    "the model. Each compulsory field is commented with its purpose and typical\n",
    "value range.\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "170f4bc4",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "# COMPULSORY: Training / hyperparameter-tuning configuration\n",
    "# =============================================================================\n",
    "training_args = SFTConfig(\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: where checkpoints + logs are written (must match OUTPUT_DIR).\n",
    "    output_dir=OUTPUT_DIR,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: number of full passes over the training dataset.\n",
    "    # 1-3 epochs is typical for instruction fine-tuning to avoid overfitting.\n",
    "    num_train_epochs={{NUM_TRAIN_EPOCHS}},\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: batch size per GPU device. Reduce if you hit CUDA OOM errors.\n",
    "    per_device_train_batch_size={{PER_DEVICE_TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE}},\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: number of steps to accumulate gradients before an optimizer\n",
    "    # step. Effective batch size = per_device_train_batch_size * this value.\n",
    "    # Use this to simulate a larger batch size on limited VRAM.\n",
    "    gradient_accumulation_steps={{GRADIENT_ACCUMULATION_STEPS}},\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: optimizer. \"paged_adamw_32bit\" is memory-efficient and\n",
    "    # recommended when using 4-bit/8-bit quantized models.\n",
    "    optim=\"paged_adamw_32bit\",\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: how often (in steps) to log training metrics.\n",
    "    logging_steps=10,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: how often (in steps) to save a checkpoint.\n",
    "    save_steps=50,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: learning rate — the single most impactful tuning parameter.\n",
    "    # Typical LoRA fine-tuning range: 1e-4 to 3e-4.\n",
    "    learning_rate={{LEARNING_RATE}},\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: max gradient norm for gradient clipping (prevents exploding\n",
    "    # gradients).\n",
    "    max_grad_norm=0.3,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: fraction of total training steps used to linearly warm up\n",
    "    # the learning rate from 0 to the target learning_rate.\n",
    "    warmup_ratio=0.03,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: learning-rate schedule shape after warmup.\n",
    "    # \"cosine\" smoothly decays LR to 0; \"constant\" and \"linear\" are alternatives.\n",
    "    lr_scheduler_type=\"{{LR_SCHEDULER_TYPE}}\",\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: use mixed precision (bf16) if the GPU supports it (A100/T4\n",
    "    # support bf16; older GPUs may need fp16=True, bf16=False instead).\n",
    "    bf16=True,\n",
    "    fp16=False,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: reduces memory usage by not storing all activations during\n",
    "    # the forward pass (recomputes them during backward pass instead).\n",
    "    gradient_checkpointing=True,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: maximum tokenized sequence length (must match MAX_SEQ_LENGTH).\n",
    "    max_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # COMPULSORY: which column in the dataset holds the training text\n",
    "    # (must match DATASET_TEXT_FIELD).\n",
    "    dataset_text_field=DATASET_TEXT_FIELD,\n",
    "\n",
    "    # Disables external experiment-tracking integrations by default.\n",
    "    # Set to \"wandb\" if you logged in above and want live dashboards.\n",
    "    report_to=\"none\",\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(\"Training arguments configured.\")\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "e22ac582",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## 8. Build the Trainer and Start Fine-Tuning"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "51e59933",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "trainer = SFTTrainer(\n",
    "    model=model,\n",
    "    args=training_args,\n",
    "    train_dataset=dataset,\n",
    "    formatting_func=formatting_func,   # None if dataset already has a \"text\" field\n",
    "    processing_class=tokenizer,\n",
    "    peft_config=lora_config,\n",
    ")\n"
   ]

    "## 14. Deploy Permanently to a Free Browser Host (Hugging Face Spaces)\n",
    "\n",
    "This section publishes your fine-tuned model to **Hugging Face Spaces**, a\n",
    "free-tier hosting platform for ML demos. Unlike the temporary link in\n",
    "Section 13, this gives you a **permanent URL** that keeps working after this\n",
    "Colab notebook is closed, e.g.:\n",
    "\n",
    "```\n",
    "https://huggingface.co/spaces/<your-username>/<your-space-name>\n",
    "```\n",
    "\n",
    "### How it works\n",
    "1. We merge the LoRA adapter into the base model (if not already done) so the\n",
    "   Space doesn't need to juggle adapters at inference time.\n",
    "2. We push that merged model to the Hugging Face **Hub** (model storage).\n",
    "3. We generate an `app.py` (Gradio web app) and `requirements.txt`.\n",
    "4. We create a Hugging Face **Space** (free `cpu-basic` tier by default) and\n",
    "   upload those two files. Hugging Face automatically builds and hosts the\n",
    "   app — no server management required on your side.\n",
    "\n",
    "### Prerequisites\n",
    "- You must be logged in to the Hugging Face Hub (Section 2 — `login()` /\n",
    "  `notebook_login()`), with a token that has **write** access.\n",
    "- Your Hugging Face account, not just a token — Spaces are created under\n",
    "  your username (or an organization you belong to)."
   ]

   "source": [
    "### 14.4 Write the Gradio app (`app.py`) and `requirements.txt`\n",
    "\n",
    "These two files are all Hugging Face Spaces needs to build and serve your model."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "ed4657cd",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "%%writefile app.py\n",
    "\"\"\"\n",
    "Gradio web app for the Knatware fine-tuned LLM.\n",
    "This file is uploaded to a Hugging Face Space and run there directly — it\n",
    "does NOT run inside this Colab notebook. Hugging Face installs\n",
    "`requirements.txt` and then executes this script automatically.\n",
    "\"\"\"\n",
    "\n",
    "import os\n",
    "import torch\n",
    "import gradio as gr\n",
    "from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline\n",
    "\n",
    "# Model repo id is injected at deploy time (see Section 14.5) via an\n",
    "# environment variable so this file doesn't need to be regenerated if you\n",
    "# retrain and push a new model version under the same repo id.\n",
    "MODEL_REPO_ID = os.environ.get(\"MODEL_REPO_ID\", \"REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_MODEL_REPO_ID\")\n",
    "\n",
    "print(f\"Loading model: {MODEL_REPO_ID}\")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Free-tier Spaces are CPU-only by default, so we fall back gracefully:\n",
    "# GPU + bfloat16 if a GPU is available (e.g. on a paid Space), else CPU + float32.\n",
    "device = \"cuda\" if torch.cuda.is_available() else \"cpu\"\n",
    "dtype = torch.bfloat16 if device == \"cuda\" else torch.float32\n",
    "\n",
    "tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_REPO_ID)\n",
    "if tokenizer.pad_token is None:\n",
    "    tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token\n",
    "\n",
    "model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n",
    "    MODEL_REPO_ID,\n",
    "    torch_dtype=dtype,\n",
    "    device_map=\"auto\" if device == \"cuda\" else None,\n",
    ")\n",
    "if device == \"cpu\":\n",
    "    model.to(device)\n",
    "\n",
    "generator = pipeline(\"text-generation\", model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, device_map=\"auto\" if device == \"cuda\" else None)\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "def respond(message, history, max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p):\n",
    "    \"\"\"Builds a prompt from the chat history and generates the next reply.\"\"\"\n",
    "    prompt = f\"### Instruction:\\n{message}\\n\\n### Response:\\n\"\n",
    "\n",
    "    output = generator(\n",
    "        prompt,\n",
    "        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,\n",
    "        do_sample=temperature > 0,\n",
    "        temperature=max(temperature, 0.01),\n",
    "        top_p=top_p,\n",
    "        pad_token_id=tokenizer.pad_token_id,\n",
    "    )\n",
    "    full_text = output[0][\"generated_text\"]\n",
    "    return full_text[len(prompt):].strip()\n",
    "\n",
    "\n",
    "with gr.Blocks(title=\"Knatware LLM Demo\") as demo:\n",
    "    gr.Markdown(\n",
    "        f\"\"\"# 🔧 Knatware Fine-Tuned LLM\n",
    "Live demo of a model fine-tuned with the Knatware LLM pipeline.\n",
    "Model: `{MODEL_REPO_ID}`\n",
    "\n",
    "*Running on a free-tier CPU Space — replies may take a little while.*\"\"\"\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "    with gr.Accordion(\"Generation settings\", open=False):\n",
    "        max_new_tokens = gr.Slider(16, 512, value=200, step=8, label=\"Max new tokens\")\n",
    "        temperature = gr.Slider(0.0, 1.5, value=0.7, step=0.05, label=\"Temperature\")\n",
    "        top_p = gr.Slider(0.1, 1.0, value=0.9, step=0.05, label=\"Top-p\")\n",
    "\n",
    "    chat = gr.ChatInterface(\n",
    "        fn=respond,\n",
    "        additional_inputs=[max_new_tokens, temperature, top_p],\n",
    "    )\n",
    "\n",
    "if __name__ == \"__main__\":\n",
    "    # Spaces expect the app to bind to 0.0.0.0:7860 by default; Gradio's\n",
    "    # default launch() already does this correctly on Spaces.\n",
    "    demo.launch()\n"
   ]
  },

   "source": [
    "### 14.5 Create the Space and upload the files\n",
    "\n",
    "This is the step that actually goes live — after it finishes, your permanent link is ready."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "16c0e624",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "from huggingface_hub import HfApi\n",
    "\n",
    "api = HfApi()\n",
    "\n",
    "# Create (or reuse, if it already exists) the Space repo.\n",
    "space_repo_id = f\"{HF_USERNAME}/{SPACE_NAME}\"\n",
    "\n",
    "api.create_repo(\n",
    "    repo_id=space_repo_id,\n",
    "    repo_type=\"space\",\n",
    "    space_sdk=\"gradio\",\n",
    "    private=not SPACE_PUBLIC,\n",
    "    exist_ok=True,          # safe to re-run; won't error if the Space exists\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Tell the Space (via a repo secret) which model to load, so app.py never\n",
    "# has to be edited/re-uploaded again if you retrain and push a v2 model to\n",
    "# the same DEPLOY_MODEL_REPO_ID.\n",
    "api.add_space_secret(\n",
    "    repo_id=space_repo_id,\n",
    "    key=\"MODEL_REPO_ID\",\n",
    "    value=DEPLOY_MODEL_REPO_ID,\n",
    ")\n",
    "\n",
    "# Upload the app + requirements. Hugging Face automatically detects the\n",
    "# push, builds a container, installs requirements.txt, and starts app.py.\n",
    "api.upload_file(\n",
    "    path_or_fileobj=\"app.py\",\n",
    "    path_in_repo=\"app.py\",\n",

// --- helpers to turn a form value into a valid Python literal, safely
//     embedded inside the notebook's own already-serialized JSON text ------

function pyString(v, fallback) {
  const s = (v === undefined || v === null || v === "") ? fallback : String(v);
  const pythonSourceText = JSON.stringify(s).slice(1, -1);
  return JSON.stringify(pythonSourceText).slice(1, -1);
}

function pyNumber(v, fallback) {
  const n = (v === undefined || v === null || v === "") ? fallback : v;
  return String(n);
}

function pyBool(v, fallback) {
  const s = (v === undefined || v === null || v === "") ? fallback : String(v);
  return (s === "Yes" || s === "true" || s === "True" || s === true) ? "True" : "False";
}

function pyList(v, fallback) {
  const raw = (v === undefined || v === null || v === "") ? fallback : String(v);
  const items = raw.split(",").map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
  const listLiteral = "[" + items.map(i => `"${i}"`).join(", ") + "]";
  return JSON.stringify(listLiteral).slice(1, -1);
}
